The remaining carbon oxides in the gas stream (Stream 13) are converted to methane in the methanation reactor and the water produced from the methanation reaction is removed from the gas stream as well. The resulting stream (Stream 14), primarily H and N , is compressed to 13.8 MPa (2,000 psia) 2 2 (Stream 15) before entering the ammonia synthesis loop. The NH formed is cooled and 3 57 COMPARISON OF COMMERCIAL, STATE-OF-THE-ART, FOSSIL-BASED AMMONIA PRODUCTION condensed then separated via flash tanks within the ammonia synthesis loop and, due to the low single-pass conversion of about 20 percent, the unreacted components are recycled back to the reactor. The purged stream (Stream 16), which is necessary to prevent the buildup of argon, nitrogen, methane, and higher hydrocarbons in the synthesis loop, is sent through a series of H 2 recovery membranes, which recover H (Stream 17) to be recycled back to the H /N 2 2 2 compressor. The ammonia-rich stream exiting the synthesis loop is further purified via flash separation and the impurities go through a water wash step that recovers additional NH 3 product. The ammonia product (Stream 18) is produced at a temperature of -33 °C (-27 °F), pressure of 0.14 MPa (20 psia), and purity of >99.9 wt% and is ready for storage in an atmospheric insulated cylindrical tank. The separation via flash tanks and the cooling of the ammonia product requires a refrigeration utility. Retentate gas from the H membrane and remaining components following ammonia 2 purification are mixed with the supplemental natural gas to form fuel gas (Stream 19) used in the reformer. The flue gas goes through convective heat recovery, which generates steam and provides heat to other parts of the plant, resulting in a cooled flue gas (Stream 20) that is sent to the Shell CANSOLV post-combustion CO capture system, which removes 97 percent of the 2 CO (Stream 21), which is sent to CO compression and drying. The clean flue gas (Stream 22) is 2 2 sent to the stack. In the CO compression and drying step, a vent from the triethylene glycol 2 dryer (Stream 23) is sent to the stack. The stack (Stream 24) vents to the atmosphere. The CO 2 product (Stream 25) is compressed to 15.3 MPa (2,214.7 psia). The plant produces steam (Stream 26) at 510 °C (950 °F) and 10.7 MPa (1,550 psia). After being sent through the HP steam turbine, a portion is sent to the primary reformer and the remaining (Stream 27) is sent through a MP steam turbine.
